text:
aaron-support: FYI — customer @jordan (acct acme-ops) reports websocket streaming disconnects from our Private/VPC deployment. Symptoms: stream starts, then connection drops around 60–70s. Our side logs show `upstream closed connection`. They route egress through a corporate middlebox/NAT.

ben-onduty: Can you paste repro steps and any client-side tcpdump or logs?

customer-jordan: Repro steps: `wscat -c "wss://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=gpt-x"` -> send prompt -> stream begins -> drops at ~65s. From our tcpdump the FIN/ACK comes from 10.0.1.1 at ~65s. No TLS alerts. Also tried `curl --no-buffer` against a streaming endpoint and saw the proxy buffer until connection close.

aaron-support: Thanks. They say no nginx reverse-proxy on their side but corporate security box likely doing DPI/idle timeouts.

sophie-sre: Most likely middlebox idle-timeout or HTTP buffering behavior. Quick checklist: 1) confirm tcpdump shows FIN/RST source (you're seeing 10.0.1.1?) 2) check our ingress logs for 499/502 matching times 3) try app-level websocket pings or enable TCP keepalive to verify. Also verify TLS SNI (some firewalls do SNI-based allowlists).

maria-eng-runtime: On our end we flush token chunks as they are generated, but some middleboxes buffer chunked/streamed responses until Content-Length or connection close. For websockets, if the TCP idle timeout is hit mid-stream the box will drop the connection. Recommend keepalives/pings.

customer-jordan: Confirmed: when we run wscat with a 20s ping interval it stays connected >10m. With default (no pings) it drops at ~65s. So keepalive mitigates.

sophie-sre: Good repro. Mitigations we should recommend to customers: - implement app-level websocket pings every 20–25s - enable OS-level TCP keepalive with short intervals - if there is an edge proxy (nginx/HAProxy), set `proxy_buffering off` and increase `proxy_read_timeout`/`proxy_send_timeout` - for AWS ALB, raise `idle_timeout` > 60s - ask corporate security to either whitelist streaming host or raise idle timeout / disable buffering for that host.

ben-onduty: Action items: 1) I'll add a KB article with troubleshooting steps and canned responses. 2) @maria any chance to expose an opt-in server-side heartbeat or diagnostic header to help debug?

maria-eng-runtime: We can add an opt-in heartbeat, but prefer SDK/client-level ping settings to avoid extra traffic for all users. We'll add `X-Redwood-Stream-Diagnostic` header emission in logs and an SDK option for auto-ping. Also will document enabling TCP keepalive and recommended values.

aaron-support: Escalating to L3 — opened internal ticket INF-4321 with attached customer pcap and our ingress logs. Assigned to @maria and @sophie. Please follow up with customer for firewall/SNI checks.

devops-bot: Support ticket INF-4321 created by aaron-support. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.internal/browse/INF-4321 :white_check_mark:

customer-jordan: Thanks team — I'll engage our network/security team to whitelist or bump idle timeout and will test the keepalive workaround today. Appreciate the prompt help. :thumbsup:

sophie-sre: Follow-up: we'll add a section to Private deployment onboarding checklist about firewall idle timeouts, proxy buffering, ALB idle timers, and include sample commands for wscat/python/node that show recommended ping intervals.

ben-onduty: I'll draft the KB and include this thread + sample tcpdump snippets and the customer pcap in INF-4321.

maria-eng-runtime: Marking for postmortem-style doc addition: "Streaming over Private/VPC — middlebox handling & best practices". Will link to INF-4321 when done.
